alignments.note: Anarthrous dative of time; the supplied *in* realizes the case and stays with the noun under rule 21's determinerless clause, discontinuously around the possessive under rule 15.
Rule 47: anarthrous ἴδιος carries the supplied possessive *its own*, headed on *own*; no article competes here. ASV margin: *his*.
Future indicative with its supplied subject and auxiliary under rule 9, headed on the lexical verb.

Rule 92: where the ASV recasts an appositional phrase with an expressed predicate noun as a finite relative clause, the article keeps only the determiner *the* and the noun carries the supplied relativizer and copula.
Expressed predicate noun carrying the supplied *who is* under rule 92, discontinuously under rule 15, headed on the noun.

Article before the substantival participle; the ASV compresses the phrase into the bare noun *kings* with no determiner for the article to anchor, so rule 23 empties it and the case preposition stays with the participle under rule 21.
Substantival participle compressed into *of kings* (ASV margin: Greek them that reign as kings); the case preposition rides with it under rule 21's determinerless clause.
Article before the second substantival participle, emptied for the same reason as s012.
Substantival participle compressed into *of lords* (ASV margin: Greek them that rule as lords).

review_notes: The *who is* of t009–t010 goes to the expressed predicate noun δυνάστης under rule 92 rather than to the article, which keeps only its own *the*.

The two participial genitives are compressed into bare nouns, so their articles have no determiner to anchor and are `unrepresented` under rule 23; rule 90's single-word case does not reach them, the one English word being the participle's own lexical realization.
